changes_vs_current: New topic. Five ranked people sources averaged (ABC 1000-year open-ended, ABC century open-ended, YouGov Ratings, Gallup century 'admire most', Wikipedia pageviews); the two 20th-century-only sources were applied only to 20th-century figures. Raw order: JFK 3.8, Lincoln 4.5, MLK 5.6, FDR 6.7, Einstein 7.9, Washington 8.8, Jesus 10.7, Churchill 13.1, Hitler 13.1, Gandhi 13.7, Napoleon 14.3, Reagan 15.0, John Paul II 16.4, Mother Teresa 17.1, Cleopatra 17.7, T. Roosevelt 17.9, Newton 18.7, Queen Victoria 19.0, Jefferson 20.3, Eisenhower 20.5, Henry VIII 21.0, Elizabeth II 21.2, Columbus 22.7, Stalin 23.0, Diana 23.2, Franklin 23.3, Marie Antoinette 23.7, Caesar 24.3. Moves: Lincoln, Washington, MLK above JFK (the all-era open-ended question and YouGov 2026 'greatest American' both put them 1-3; JFK's lead comes from century-only questions; JFK to 6, FDR to 7); Jesus 7 to 4 (top open-ended dinner pick, YouGov Ratings #8, named even in a 1000-year question outside his era); Benjamin Franklin 26 to 12 (YouGov Ratings #7, fame 97%; raw score hurt because century sources can't include him); Jefferson 19 to 13 (YouGov #15, ABC 2%); Columbus 23 to 14 (ABC 2%, 21% greatest explorer); Julius Caesar 28 to 17 (ABC 1% despite era, 98% awareness, pageviews #30). Queen Victoria and Henry VIII dropped (only English Wikipedia pageviews, British-leaning; no US poll names them), freeing spots for Eisenhower, Elizabeth II and Stalin. Bare 'Roosevelt' is on neither Roosevelt (ambiguous).
confidence: Medium. Top 5 (Lincoln, Washington, MLK, Jesus, Einstein) strong. Positions 6-14 solid as a set, order soft. The main open-ended US polls are from 1999 and lean toward 20th-century Americans and presidents (overlaps the US Presidents topic, but reflects what people say). YouGov Ratings sorts by popularity, so Hitler and Stalin get no credit there. Cleopatra's 2025 pageviews look inflated. Spots 22-24 weak. Near misses: Rosa Parks, Shakespeare, Anne Frank, Leonardo da Vinci, Alexander the Great, Nelson Mandela, Princess Diana, Queen Victoria, Henry VIII, Genghis Khan, Thomas Edison, Eleanor Roosevelt, Helen Keller.
